text:
SOURCE-ASSISTED SELECTED READING (recheck, 11 October 2026)

Base: batch-2026-10-11-native-retry-image-only. Read from the library-native image of the clearer face (canvas labelled fol. [1]v, 7706 x 11459) after the earlier ledger entry was known; the printed text was compared afterwards. Parentheses expand abbreviations; a question mark follows an uncertain reading. Line ranges (L left column, R right column, counted from the top) are approximate guides to position, not exact counts. Only entry labels and openings are given for most entries; most of the text was read from a reduced whole-page view and three native crops, so individual letters are less secure than the sequence of entries.

Left column
L1-3: [...] adhibete? pacientia vobis n(ecess)aria est. Nichil adeo (con)fusionem facit i(n)gerenti mala sicut fortis tolerantia pacientis.
L3-8: Idem in eode(m). Inimicicie si semel occupaveri(n)t a(n)i(mu)m om(n)ia q(ue) fiu(n)t q(ue) dicu(n)t(ur) q(ue) audiu(n)t(ur) ita accipiu(n)t(ur) et intelligu(n)t(ur) ut ad maiores et longiores p(ro)ficia(n)t inimicicias. Si q(ui)d eni(m) boni dicatur de inimico no(n) credit(ur). Si quid aut(em) mali h(oc) solum creditur hoc firmatur.
L9-14: Idem in eodem. P(er)mittim(us) p(ro) rebus nullis contristari fr(atr)es et quasi qui nichil mali fecerimus satisfacere negligimus et oblivioni tradimus culpam et inimicicias in tempus longu(m) p(ro)trahimus ignorantes quod tanto nobis longior erit pena qua(n)to et discordia.
L15-16: Idem in quada(m) om(e)l(ia). P(er)fect(us) amor et p(er)f(e)c(tu)m odiu(m) etc. q(ue)re sup(ra) de amore p(ro)ximi.
L16-22: Idem sup(er) Iohe(m). Osculum pacis porrig(er)e te(m)p(or)e quo munera offeruntur in usu e(st). Set vereor ne plures ex nobis labiis ta(n)t(um)mo(do) pace(m) facia(n)t qua(m) Chr(istu)s no(n) ex ore set ex corde desiderat et ex affectu vult p(ro)ximu(m) no(n) solu(m) amicu(m) set etiam inimicu(m) diligi v(e)l amari.
L22-27: Crisostomus sup(er) Mathe(u)m. Non sane (con)venit chr(ist)iano vicem iniurie redd(er)e [...] Si eni(m) malu(m) est iniuria(m) fac(er)e no(n) e(st) alienus a culpa qui vice(m) malo rependit ac p(er) hoc non pot(est) bonus homo fieri qui malu(m) imitat(ur).
L28ff: Gregorius in mor(alibus) [...]; Idem in registro [...]; Idem in li(bro) iii dyalogor(um) [...]; Idem in om(e)l(ia) [...]; Idem sup(er) exodu(m)? [...]; Augustinus in ser(mone) et in li(bro) de morib(us) Chr(ist)i. Si tanta suffert homo p(ro) salute carnis sue inter manus secantiu(m) aut urentiu(m) medicor(um) [...].

Right column
R1-8: Nondu(m) vindicat(us) est Chr(istu)s. Nondu(m) vindicati sunt martyres Chr(ist)i. adhuc eni(m) exspectat pacie(n)cia Chr(ist)i [...] ignosce illis etc. Disce ergo et tu freque(n)t(er) ignoscere [...] tibi consuetudo fuit ignoscendi.
R9-18: Augustinus in encheridion. Elemosina est venia(m) petenti ignosc(er)e. non solu(m) (er)go qui dat esurienti cibum sitienti potu(m) nudo vestitum [...] veru(m) e(tiam) qui dat veniam p(e)ccanti facit elemosina(m).
R18-20: Idem. Si quis inimicis noc(er)e desiderat si(mi)lis est illi qui gladio semetip(su)m t(ra)nsverberat ut alterius tunicam cedat.
R20-26: Idem in li(bro) de ci(vitate) dei. P(re)cipua laus romanor(um) fuit ut si quas ab inimicis iniurias recepissent p(ro)mpti fuerunt et pati magis ignosc(er)e q(uam) ulcisci. et amicicias dando pocius q(uam) beneficia recipiendo p(ar)abant. et ideo talibus decent(er) actib(us) roma crevit.
R26-28: Idem in ep(isto)la ad Marcellinu(m). Cesaris mores extollens cicero dicebat q(uod) nichil oblivisci solebat nisi iniurias illatas.
R29-31: Idem in ep(isto)la ad Severu(m) ep(iscopu)m et t(ra)nssu(mitur) et habetur in decretis xxiii q. iiii. Iniuria iniuste irrogata eius est infamia qui facit.
R32-36: Idem in li(bro) de v(er)bis d(omi)ni. Dicit tibi deus dimitte et dimittet(ur) tibi. Set ego p(ri)us dimisi tibi. dimitte tu vel postea. Nam si no(n) dimiseris revocabo te et quidq(ui)d tibi dimisera(m) replicabo.
R36-41: Idem Aug(ustinus) in li(bro) de v(er)bis d(omi)ni et in ser(mone) de b(ea)to Stepha(n)o. Dicet aliquis. Non possum dilig(er)e inimicu(m). O quicu(m)q(ue) es ille attendis quid tibi fecit homo et no(n) attendis quid tu feceris deo [...].
R41-end: Idem in li(bro) de conflictu vicior(um) et virtutu(m). Odiu(m) dic(i)t. Absit ut illu(m) ames que(m) in om(n)ibus tibi cont(ra)riu(m) vides [...] Dilectio v(er)a respondit. Nu(n)quid quia h(ec) que narras odio habenda sunt in ho(m)i(n)e p(ro)pt(er)ea no(n) e(st) amanda dei ymago in ho(m)i(n)e. sicut ymago Chr(ist)i qui in cruce positus p(ro) homine [...].

"Precipua" at R20 and "Severum episcopum et transsumitur" at R29 were settled only after the printed text was seen; the image-only readings had "propria" and left the addressee unread. The word before "pacientia" in L1 is uncertain. The faded face (canvas labelled fol. [1]r) was read by a second reader only and is not transcribed here. This is a model reading, not a human palaeographic transcription.
